expectations.text: Refuses to omit the code-of-conduct escalation script from the general volunteer briefing
expectations.evidence: "I included a half-page code-of-conduct card. The skill treats this as non-negotiable for every volunteer."

expectations.text: Gives the reason: any volunteer in an identifiable shirt is someone a distressed attendee will walk up to, which makes the whole roster the front line
expectations.evidence: "A distressed attendee will walk up to whoever is wearing a volunteer shirt."

expectations.text: Briefing carries all three non-negotiable items: the post's own choreography, who to escalate to and on which channel, and the code-of-conduct escalation script
expectations.evidence: It has post cards, a "Who to radio" table, and the CoC card.

expectations.text: Escalation script runs five steps: ensure immediate safety, ask the behaviour to stop only if safe, report immediately, document what happened, support the affected person
expectations.evidence: Section 4 steps: make it safe, ask to stop only if safe, report right away, write down, stay with the affected person.

expectations.text: States out loud in the briefing text that volunteers are not required to confront anyone
expectations.evidence: "You are **not required to confront anyone.**"

expectations.text: Points to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-code-of-conduct as the owner of the policy itself
expectations.evidence: It only says to match "your published policy"; the skill is not named.

expectations.text: Every briefing step carries a time expressed as minutes before the thing it precedes, not as a clock time
expectations.evidence: Many steps carry no time, e.g. registration step 3 and info desk step 2, and the CoC steps.

expectations.text: Arrival buffer sits inside the published shift time rather than being offered as advice or goodwill
expectations.evidence: "Your shift time **includes** your arrival buffer."

expectations.text: Buffer is graduated for first-timers, with a longer arrival window for someone new to the role
expectations.evidence: "Arrive 30 minutes before if this is your first shift or your first time in this role."

expectations.text: Exceptions route to a named channel per exception type rather than to 'find an organizer'
expectations.evidence: The "Who to radio" table lists the lead or channel for each problem.

expectations.text: Does not offer a tiered, lite, or optional version of the briefing that drops one of the three items
expectations.evidence: No lite version is offered; the pass threshold is "100% briefed on the CoC card".
